LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – SHORT STORIES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are short stories important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition
2. use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – SHORT STORIES
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING – SHORT STORIES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction

What this means
In this part you learn to use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories to a partner. (skill: use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition.
3. Practise this skill: use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are short stories important?
2. Why is it important to ensure safety in your environment and especially roads?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Extensive reading – short stories means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary from texts on the theme for language acquisition.
5. Be able to: use vocabulary related to the theme for sentence construction.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
